newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: IMF chief praises Mozambique's economic progress.
newsitem.headline: IMF chief praises Mozambique's economic progress.

text.p: Mozambique is making good economic progress and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) could include it in a new debt reduction initiative, IMF managing director Michel Camdessus was quoted as saying on Thursday.
The Portuguese news agency Lusa, reporting from the Mozambican capital Maputo, said Camdessus had been "positively impressed" by the results of the country's economic reforms.
He said inflation should be below Mozambique's 1996 target of 22 percent by the end of the year.

"I hope that next year the IMF board will take an irrevocable decision to make Mozambique eligible for the benefits of this special initiative," Camdessus told a news conference at the end of a two-day visit.
"Despite the big financial problems involved, we finally succeeded in getting absolute consensus from the international community to support this initiative," Camdessus said.
He gave no further details of the new initiative and said it was not possible to say what percentage of Mozambique's debt would be covered by the scheme.
Mozambique's foreign debt stands at around $5.5 billion, a level which the World Bank and IMF say is unsustainable.
